accuracy.evidence: Matches the national curriculum for English, Years 5 and 6 writing: plan by noting and developing initial ideas, drawing on reading; in narratives, consider how authors have developed characters and settings in what pupils have read; describe settings, characters and atmosphere. Show-don't-tell, character methods (action, speech, thought, appearance), setting-as-mood and the wide-to-close 'camera zoom' are standard KS2 craft terms used in Bitesize and EEF writing guidance. The mentor paragraph (Nell), the Jay notes and the zoom lines are original, so nothing is quoted from a copyrighted book.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets known slips: naming the trait in the plan (Telling bin, 'Jay is brave but scared' note, m2, sorter), intensifiers as a fix ('very, very nervous' prediction, m5), treating speech as truth (Nell's 'not scared' prediction, m3), mixing moods (cheerful chips, p4), setting as only 'where' (prediction), copying mentor sentences (challenge 'copy' tag, m6) and plot-only plans (m8, adult text).

lab_distinct.evidence: Mechanics are specific to planning from a mentor text: a dealt deck of lines into telling/showing bins, tap-to-cycle method labels on a mentor paragraph, a three-slot character plan that rejects telling, contradictory and irrelevant notes with their own reasons, a mood board that rejects cheerful and mood-naming chips, and a drag-swap wide-to-close zoom. It shares no step with the plot-structure or writing-process labs.

lab_teaches.evidence: Each step makes the learner do the skill: sorting shows why named feelings tell; labelling Nell's lines reveals the gap between speech and thought; the plan slots only accept details that show Jay's trait and say why others fail; the mood board explains why a cheerful or 'very scary' note breaks the mood; swapping the zoom lines states the wide-then-closer rule. Completion messages restate the method.

predictions.evidence: Three predictions with tempting wrong answers that the next task disproves: 'very, very nervous' as the stronger line, believing Nell because she says she is not scared, and setting as 'just where it happens'.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Seven challenge items with rotating answer positions. Each wrong option carries a tag with its own message (tell, fact, method, mood, copy, zoom); the answer is shown after a miss and the canvas keeps a three-point method summary on screen.

readability.evidence: Learner text passes the repo's Flesch-Kincaid limit for kid text and adult text the 9.5 limit. Sentences are short, terms (mentor text, show, mood, zoom) are explained with an example on first use, and lab lines are one or two sentences.

no_filler.evidence: Every paragraph teaches a method the lab uses or names mistakes; the adult text gives concrete checks for a plan. Lab copy is instructions and feedback only, and no gate filler phrase matches.

mobile.evidence: Checked on iPhone 13 screenshots: two large bins with a full-width dealt card, four full-width mentor lines with label pills, three plan slots over a two-column note tray, a mood plan over two columns of chips, and four zoom rows with size dots. Text wraps inside each card and buttons below the canvas are at least 44 px.

accessibility.evidence: Every drag has a button twin: Telling/Showing, 'Label line N', 'Note N' then 'Put in Action/Speech/Thought', 'Add N' and '↑ Line N', all with full text in aria-labels. The canvas aria-label reports bin counts, labels, slots, the mood plan or the zoom order after each action. axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) is clean in both themes on desktop and iPhone.
